headline: Committee adds ʻulu tree and monkeypod grove to exceptional trees list

meeting.summary: The committee approved an ʻulu tree and 22 monkeypods as exceptional trees and heard testimony against a subdivision board's tree removal plan.
meeting.recap: The committee reached a quorum, meaning enough members were present to meet.[[0:01:18]] A homeowner testified against a subdivision board's plan to remove trees.[[0:01:40]] A letter to the subdivision's board will go on the August agenda for the committee to approve.[[0:13:46]] No one will enter the banyan tree's park for two years so the tree can heal.[[0:17:25]] The chair said he knows of no current permit process for trimming exceptional trees.[[0:31:42]] Members agreed that people should tell the committee who will trim an exceptional tree and when.[[0:43:01]] The committee voted to make an ʻulu tree next to a fire station an exceptional tree.[[0:44:55]] The committee approved 22 monkeypod trees in a University of Hawaiʻi Maui campus parking lot as exceptional trees.[[0:45:11]] A member said his group bought materials to fence the entire burn scar to keep deer out.[[0:52:08]] The next meeting is August 12th, 2026 at 1:30 p.m.[[0:57:24]]
decided: The committee approved making the ʻulu tree next to the fire station an exceptional tree, with no objections heard.
The chair declared unanimous consent to add 22 monkeypod trees in a campus parking lot as exceptional trees.
Members agreed to have people trimming exceptional trees contact the committee so it can record the information.
The committee voted to adjourn the meeting.
meeting.next: The chair asked to be told of the subdivision board's next meeting so a committee member can attend. A legal adviser offered to research the trimming permit question. The exceptional tree changes will go to the county council together with the tree removals.
